title: Bárbara Mori Returns in Las Azules Season 2, Keeps Bollywood Door Open
excerpt: The Kites actress leads Apple TV's acclaimed Mexican crime drama into its second season, while her connection to Indian cinema remains a talking point for fans on both sides of the world.
body:
• Season 2 of Las Azules (Women in Blue), starring Bárbara Mori, premiered on Apple TV on August 12 with weekly episodes through September 30
  • Mori plays María, now promoted to lieutenant, in the acclaimed Spanish-language crime drama set in 1970s Mexico
  • The series holds a 100% rating on Rotten Tomatoes for its first season and is Apple TV's first original production in Latin America
  • Mori, who starred opposite Hrithik Roshan in Kites (2010), has previously expressed her desire to do more films in India

Women in Blue Returns

https://youtube.com/watch?v=Z9n3TkdcGLY

Bárbara Mori is back as the fierce María in Season 2 of Las Azules (Women in Blue), the Apple TV crime drama that premiered its sophomore run on August 12 with eight weekly episodes running through September 30.

The Spanish-language series, which earned a perfect 100% score on Rotten Tomatoes for its first season, returns with a storyline woven around two of Mexico's most traumatic historical events — the 1968 Tlatelolco massacre and the 1971 Halcones attack on student protesters.

"The investigation is going to delve deeply into the subject, not just the institution of the police force itself, but also the 1971 student massacre, bringing all of that back into the present to see what was behind it all," Mori told Reuters. "It's a pretty intense season, just talking about it gives me goosebumps."

A Darker, More Complex Season

Season 2 picks up a day after Los Halcones, a paramilitary force, attacked a student protest in Mexico City in June 1971, killing or wounding dozens. When a young man is found dead in murky circumstances, the four Azules — María, Valentina, Gabina, and Ángeles — are pulled into an investigation that points to corruption within the police force itself and ties back to the 1968 massacre.

https://x.com/IndiaToday/status/2089220995412574441

María, now promoted to lieutenant, finds herself torn between duty and truth. Co-creator Fernando Rovzar, who is also Mori's husband, described the season as a test of the characters' moral compass.

"Do they defend the system that they know is wrong or do they defend their own principles, even though they have to go against the system?"

— Fernando Rovzar, co-creator and showrunner

Ximena Sariñana, who plays Ángeles, said all four characters are "going through transitions, trying to adapt to what the expectation is of a woman in their specific situation."

Mori's Bollywood Connection

For Indian audiences, Mori is best known for starring opposite Hrithik Roshan in Kites (2010), the Rakesh Roshan-produced cross-cultural love story that was her introduction to Bollywood. The Uruguayan-born Mexican actress made a strong impression during the film's India promotions, expressing deep affection for Mumbai and Indian culture.

"I love all the Indian people. They're so lovely and so warm. They make me feel so much at home," Mori said during the Kites press tour. She also signed a second Bollywood project, the thriller Fever (2016), opposite Rajeev Khandelwal.

In interviews around Kites, Mori expressed her wish to continue working in Indian cinema: "I'd love to do many films in India," she told Filmibeat, noting that her brother had been living in Mumbai for years as a singer. She described Mexican and Indian cultures as "very similar in some ways yet very different in others."

Apple TV's Latin American Flagship

Las Azules holds the distinction of being Apple TV's first original production in Latin America, produced by Lemon Studios. Created by International Emmy winner Rovzar and Pablo Aramendi, the series features an entirely Latin American cast and crew.

Rovzar has signaled interest in continuing the story beyond Season 2. "There's so many stories we can still tackle, issues from the past that are also relevant today," he told Reuters. "The pen's in my hand and I'm ready for another one."

Where to Watch

Season 2 of Women in Blue (Las Azules) is streaming on Apple TV with new episodes every Wednesday through September 30. The complete first season is also available on the platform. The series is available in Spanish with English subtitles and dubbed versions.
